system: You are a Python programmer. Return only the modified score function.
prompt_template:
Modify this bin-scoring function to reduce the number of bins used in online bin packing. Keep the interface score(item, bins), and output only Python code.
item is a positive float; bins is a nonempty 1D numpy float64 array of feasible remaining capacities, each >= item. Capacity is 100. The evaluator preallocates one empty bin per item, scores all feasible bins, chooses the highest score, and breaks ties by the earliest bin index. Item order is fixed.
Return a finite numpy float64 array with exactly the same shape as bins. Use one pure deterministic function with straight-line local assignments and a return. numpy is already available as np. You may import numpy as np. Use numpy vector operations; do not use loops, helper functions, randomness, I/O, external state, or modify bins. No reflections or explanation.
Parent function:
{code}
fixed_meaningful_reason: Requested additional comparator after highest aggregate improvement in prior confirmation; does not replace original temporary baseline
selection: Two common uniform population indices with replacement; lower training mean bins wins; ties use earlier discovery
replacement: After each attempt, top 8 distinct canonical ordered trees in parent population plus valid child; training bins then discovery order; elitist
canonical_identity: Expanded ordered AST, without local names or source formatting; no algebraic/commutative simplification

candidate_contract.reason: Keep representation space closed under reproduction, bound expansion/context; same eligibility for all four methods

evaluator_changes_before_generation: Prior scorer preserved except read-only metadata and reshape/astype receivers may be derived pure array expressions, to make normalization representation-invariant

adaptive.priors: Beta(1,1) per canonical parent and representation
adaptive.warm_start: First 3 reproductions of each canonical parent use each representation once, in deterministic seed/parent-specific random order
adaptive.thereafter: Independent Beta draws; choose largest draw; ties representation order
adaptive.success: Accepted valid child with strictly fewer mean train bins than selected parent; everything else failure
adaptive.new_parent: Fresh priors for a genuinely new canonical tree; exact same tree shares its own record, including return after absence; no ancestral inheritance

random_policy: Independent uniform choice among three representations at every attempt; no forced balancing

evaluation.validation_selection: After all searches end, select lowest valid mean validation bins from each final population; training bins and discovery order break ties
evaluation.test_release: Only after all 1152 attempts and all 12 validation-selected final candidates are sealed; test those candidates only
evaluation.curve_replay: After all generation, evaluate the stored prefix populations on validation for retrospective diagnostics only, never feedback; no prefix test evaluation

pilot_gate: First seed: audit 4x96 requests, common EC, exact policy replay, Beta updates, new-parent reset, equivalent trees and train-only access; at least one valid generated child per method. Gate ignores method wins, quality ranking and learning-opportunity adequacy
continuation: If pilot structural gate passes, run the two prespecified additional seeds with no method/parameter changes; if gate fails stop for workflow diagnosis
primary_quality: Per-search validation-selected final candidate test mean bins; seed is comparison unit (n=3)
cost_definition: All 96 calls including warm trials/errors, input/output tokens, active parent/policy/transform/evaluation/update time, actual initial training evaluation and final validation selection. Test assessment and retrospective curve work reported separately
cost_comparison: Common token/time budgets within each seed; retrospective validation best-in-prefix-population. Counterfactual stop time includes measured 8-candidate validation cost at that prefix. Earliest/latest feasible prefixes chosen by cost, not quality
success_rule: Descriptive exploration support only if adaptive has strictly lower 3-seed mean final-test bins than all 3 controls AND lower paired-mean normalized validation-quality AUC versus all 3 at common token and complete algorithm time budgets. Mixed quality/cost results remain a tradeoff, not a win. No rule changes based on seed 1
inference_scope: Three seeds on one fixed new train/validation/test set, one model, eight previously outcome-selected initial rules; not confirmatory significance or broad parent/task generalization
